title: Heart, chambers and coronary vessels (posterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Forms most of the posterior surface (base) of the heart, directly in front of the esophagus.
Oxygenated blood from the four pulmonary veins.
Left ventricle, through the mitral valve.
hy: The most posterior chamber. When it enlarges, as in mitral stenosis, it can press on the esophagus (difficulty swallowing) or on the left recurrent laryngeal nerve (hoarseness).

rows: Forms the right border of the heart.
Deoxygenated blood from the superior vena cava, the inferior vena cava, and the coronary sinus.
Right ventricle, through the tricuspid valve.
hy: The sinoatrial node lies in its wall beside the opening of the superior vena cava. The atrioventricular node lies in the interatrial septum near the opening of the coronary sinus.
The fossa ovalis in the interatrial septum is the remnant of the foramen ovale.

rows: Forms the apex and the left border of the heart.
Oxygenated blood from the left atrium, through the mitral valve.
Aorta, through the aortic valve, and so to the whole body.
Most of the venous blood of the heart wall, from the great, middle, and small cardiac veins.
Lies in the posterior part of the coronary groove, between the left atrium and the left ventricle.
Right atrium, between the opening of the inferior vena cava and the tricuspid valve.
Posterior parts of both ventricles and of the interventricular septum.
Runs in the posterior interventricular groove with the posterior interventricular artery.
The parts of the heart supplied by the left coronary artery.
Ascends in the anterior interventricular groove beside the anterior interventricular artery, then runs in the coronary groove with the circumflex artery.
Left coronary artery, where it divides.
Runs in the coronary groove around the left border of the heart to its posterior surface.
Left atrium and the lateral and posterior walls of the left ventricle. In a minority of people it gives the posterior interventricular artery.
hy: Occlusion causes a lateral myocardial infarction (ST elevation in leads I, aVL, V5, and V6).

structures.name: Right coronary artery
objects: Right inferolateral branch of right coronary artery

rows: Right aortic sinus of the ascending aorta.
Runs in the coronary groove around the right border of the heart to its posterior surface.

Right atrium and most of the right ventricle. In most people it also supplies the sinoatrial node, the atrioventricular node, and, through the posterior interventricular artery, the inferior wall of the left ventricle and the posterior third of the septum.
hy: Occlusion causes an inferior myocardial infarction (ST elevation in leads II, III, and aVF), often with bradycardia or heart block because it usually supplies the nodes.

rows: Upper lobe of its lung. On the right it also drains the middle lobe.
Upper lobe of its lung. On the right it also drains the middle lobe.
